name: watchtower
label: Watchtower
description: Tell me when a page changes. Give it a URL, an optional regex to pull one value out of the page, and how often to look: when the text changes it raises a notice (and the header ticker) with the old and new value. For price drops, council bin days, release notes or a booking slot opening. Checks run on the dashboard's 10-second sampler; each watch has its own interval, and nothing is stored outside watches.json.

steps: Open Apps > Watchtower and fill in a name, the page URL and how often to look (minutes). Optionally give a regex: the first match (or its first capture group) is the value that must change, which stops adverts and timestamps from raising a false alarm. Save; the first check records a baseline silently.

On a change the watch raises a dashboard notice and a header ticker line with the old and new value - the same path as the agent's notify tool. The page keeps the last value so you can see why it fired.
The check button fetches immediately and updates the stored value, so it is also the way to re-baseline after an expected change. Deleting a watch removes it from watches.json.
fixes: The checker runs on the dashboard's 10-second sampler, not on its own timer: the app must be running and the watch's interval must have elapsed. Press check now to prove the fetch works; if that says blocked or 403, the site is refusing the request, not the watcher.
A watch fires when nothing changed

The whole page text includes timestamps, adverts and CSRF tokens. Put a regex on the value you care about (a price, a date, 'in stock') - the watcher compares only the first match or its first capture group.
A watch says the regex did not match
The regex is applied to the page with tags and scripts stripped, whitespace collapsed. Check it against that text rather than against the HTML source; a capture group is used when there is one.
